indicators.statement: City ordinance/EO creating the CDRRMO as a regular office (not ad hoc), with defined functions mirroring RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)
CDRRMC constituted with complete membership per RA 10121 Sec. 11 (incl. CSO and private sector reps)
indicators.means_of_verification: EO on CDRRMC composition; list of members

indicators.statement: CDRRMC meets at least quarterly (and as needed); minutes and resolutions on file
CDRRMO serves as CDRRMC secretariat with documented secretariat procedures
Local DRRM-related ordinances in force (e.g., pre-emptive/forced evacuation, no-build zones, hazard-based zoning)
Protocol for declaring a State of Calamity, incl. CDRRMC recommendation steps and post-declaration measures (State of Imminent Disaster now assessed separately under A1.8)
DRRM is represented in City Development Council and Local Finance Committee deliberations

State of Imminent Disaster procedure: CDRRMC coordinates with RDRRMC VIII when the pre-disaster risk assessment shows reasonable certainty of severe impact; request format to RDRRMC (24-hour reply); Mayor's EO template; adoption rule when the Region (or Province, applicability to an ICC to be confirmed) is declared; lifting grounds and authority
indicators.reference: RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 6; Rule III Secs. 2-4
indicators.means_of_verification: SOP; EO template; CDRRMC resolution and RDRRMC request templates

indicators.statement: Organizational structure follows JMC 2014-1: Head + Administration & Training, Research & Planning, and Operations & Warning divisions
CDRRMO Head is a permanent plantilla position filled by a qualified appointee
Minimum plantilla positions per JMC 2014-1 created and filled (ratio of filled/required)
Job descriptions/position descriptions defined for every position, aligned to RA 10121 functions
24/7 operations capability with documented shift roster (Operations Center/Duty officers)
Training needs analysis done and competency-based training plan for staff (ICS, BLS/SFA, WASAR, CSSR, MOSAR, EOC, PDNA, GIS)
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 14; OCD/DRRM Training Institute curricula

indicators.statement: Personnel welfare and safety: insurance, hazard pay, PPE, psychosocial support for responders
indicators.means_of_verification: Insurance policy; PPE inventory; MHPSS program

indicators.statement: Volunteer/auxiliary responder management system (accreditation, registry, deployment, insurance), incl. mobilization of ACDVs for anticipatory action
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 13; NDRRMC volunteer guidelines; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 5

indicators.statement: Anticipatory action focal person designated in the CDRRMO, with AA training for staff, BDRRMCs, ACDVs and partner CSOs (incl. community-based early warning and early action)
indicators.reference: RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 1; Rule VII

indicators.statement: Inventory of DRRM-relevant skills across the CDRRMO, partner offices and barangays (SAR, engineering, logistics, GIS, PDNA, MHPSS) updated within the last 12 months
Local DRRM Plan (LDRRMP) current, approved by Sanggunian, aligned with NDRRMP 2020-2030 and Sendai Framework
DRR-CCA mainstreamed in CDP, CLUP, ELA and LCCAP (hazard data used in land use and investment decisions)
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 2; RA 9729 as amended by RA 10174; HLURB/DHSUD CLUP guidelines

indicators.statement: Hazard-specific Contingency Plans for priority hazards (flood/flash flood, landslide, earthquake/tsunami, tropical cyclone, industrial/geothermal), updated and tested
indicators.reference: NDRRMC CP guidelines; OCD CP Manual

indicators.statement: Public Service Continuity Plan (PSCP) prepared covering CDRRMO and essential city services
Annual LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) prepared, approved and consistent with LDRRMP
Evacuation plan with mapped routes, safe zones, centers and pre-emptive evacuation triggers per barangay
Barangay DRRM plans (85 barangays) reviewed/consolidated by CDRRMO
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); DILG MC on BDRRM

indicators.statement: LDRRMF set at not less than 5% of estimated revenue from regular sources
70% Mitigation/Preparedness and 30% Quick Response Fund (QRF) allocation observed
Unexpended LDRRMF transferred to Special Trust Fund and used within 5 years
LDRRMF utilization rate monitored and reported (target >= 80% of current-year 70% fund)
Emergency procurement procedures (negotiated procurement - emergency cases) documented and pre-arranged (framework agreements, pre-qualified suppliers)

Anticipatory action funding pathway: LDRRMFIP sets an AA line within the cap of 10% of the 70% LDRRMF; other sources mapped (Special Trust Fund balances, donations, ODA); Budget, Accounting and BAC procedures allow immediate disbursement and observe the 30%/70% tranche rule around the 3-day lead time
indicators.means_of_verification: LDRRMFIP AA line; Budget/Accounting guidance; disbursement and procurement SOP

indicators.statement: Risk transfer/financing instruments explored (indemnity insurance of public assets, PSF access, partnerships)
indicators.reference: NDRRMP; RA 10174 (People's Survival Fund); DOF-BTr NIP

indicators.statement: Clean COA findings on LDRRMF in last audit year (or findings addressed)
indicators.means_of_verification: COA Annual Audit Report; action plan

indicators.statement: QRF and LDRRMF adequacy tested against the most severe credible scenario (e.g., a Thelma-type flash flood or Yolanda-strength typhoon), with the shortfall and other fund sources identified
indicators.means_of_verification: Costed scenario; LDRRMFIP; Budget Office analysis

indicators.statement: Updated hazard maps for all priority hazards (MGB, PHIVOLCS, PAGASA, GeoRiskPH/HazardHunterPH) at barangay scale
Climate & Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA)/ CRA completed with exposure (population, buildings, critical facilities) and vulnerability data
Disaggregated population database (sex, age, disability, IP, pregnant/lactating) for at-risk households

indicators.statement: DRRM information system/ database with disaster event history, damage and losses (incl. 1991 flood, 2013 Yolanda, 2017 earthquake records)
Data privacy compliance for beneficiary and affected-population data (DPO, consent, data sharing agreements)
GIS capability (software, trained staff, updated base maps) within Research & Planning
One maintained, shared source of risk and readiness information (hazard maps, plans, contacts, readiness summary) open to CDRRMC member offices, with a public summary posted

Critical facilities list (EOC, hospitals, evacuation centers, water, power, telecom, bridges, port) with dependencies mapped as potential failure chains and used to set protection and restoration priorities
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 2.3.1; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule I Sec. 5(b),(d)

indicators.statement: Agreed update cycle: hazard data every 3 years or less; exposure, vulnerability and critical-facility data every 18 months or less
indicators.means_of_verification: Update procedure; version dates of datasets

indicators.statement: Hazard-specific EWS operational for flood (incl. Anilao/Malbasag river systems), rain-induced landslide, tsunami (Ormoc Bay) and tropical cyclone
indicators.means_of_verification: EWS inventory; functionality logs; maps of sensors/gauges

indicators.statement: Warning thresholds linked to specific actions (alert levels -> pre-emptive evacuation, class/work suspension, State of Imminent Disaster request) in written protocols, built to take up NDRRMC impact-based triggers once issued
indicators.reference: RA 10121; RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 2; DILG Operation L!sto

indicators.statement: Last-mile dissemination channels tested to barangay/purok level (sirens, radio, SMS/ECBS, social media, barangay criers)
indicators.reference: RA 10639 (Free Mobile Disaster Alerts); NDRRMC EWS

indicators.statement: Warnings issued in local language (Cebuano/ Ormocanon) and accessible formats (sign language, visual alerts for PWD)
Designated public information officer and risk communication plan (incl. rumor/misinformation management)
IEC program on hazards and preparedness with annual reach targets

Templates and channels for public notice of a State of Imminent Disaster and of the anticipatory actions required, incl. sector-specific impact-based advisories and reach to geographically isolated barangays

Participation in quarterly Nationwide Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) and hazard-specific drills with evaluation

indicators.statement: Prepositioned relief stocks/food packs and non-food items with inventory and replenishment triggers

indicators.statement: Schools, hospitals and critical facilities included in preparedness planning and drills
Refresher cycle (at least annual) set for trained responders, EOC staff and BDRRMC members, with attendance tracked
BDRRMCs can account for residents of affected puroks within 12 hours of impact (welfare check), shown in a drill or a real event
indicators.means_of_verification: Drill or AAR record; barangay reports

indicators.statement: Incident Command System institutionalized: EO on ICS, trained IMT roster, pre-designated Incident Commanders
Organized and trained response teams: SAR (WASAR/CSSR/HAZMAT as relevant), EMS/ambulance, fire coordination with BFP

indicators.statement: Response equipment and vehicles inventoried, serviceable and maintained (preventive maintenance schedule)

indicators.statement: Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA) conducted before forecast hazards, with anticipatory actions recorded
indicators.reference: NDRRMC PDRA protocol; RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 5

indicators.statement: Management of the Dead and Missing (MDM) and Rapid Damage Assessment & Needs Analysis (RDANA) teams designated and trained

Anticipatory action protocols by hazard and lead time: office-order templates for prepositioning (relief, medical supplies, animal feed, water and power for evacuation centers), deployment of heavy equipment, transport and personnel, pre-emptive evacuation incl. livestock and pets, CCCM, and safeguarding of critical infrastructure; aligned with CPs, Oplan L!sto and evacuation plans

Recovery data (damage, losses, livelihood, housing) tracked to completion
Psychosocial and livelihood recovery services coordinated with CSWDO, CHO, PESO
Pre-disaster recovery framework: roles, PDNA activation, temporary shelter, debris management and recovery fund sources agreed before an event

Regular reporting to OCD Region VIII/RDRRMC and DILG (SitReps, LDRRMF reports, Operation L!sto)
Monitoring & evaluation framework for LDRRMP with indicators and annual review
Full Disclosure Policy: LDRRMF and utilization posted publicly
After-action reviews conducted after significant events and lessons integrated into plans

EOC established by EO/ordinance with defined mandate, authority and relationship to CDRRMC and ICS

indicators.statement: Activation, escalation, de-escalation and deactivation procedures with designated authority
Concept of operations documents EOC functions: coordination, information management, resource management, policy support
EOC linkage to Provincial (Leyte) and Regional (OCD VIII) EOCs defined
EOC site located outside high flood, landslide, tsunami and liquefaction zones (checked vs hazard maps)
Building structural integrity assessed (seismic - Philippine Fault proximity) and certified
Backup power (generator + fuel for >=72 hours, UPS) tested regularly
Functional layout: operations floor, briefing/decision room, comms room, rest area, sanitation, kitchen
Water, food and sanitation supplies for EOC staff for >=72 hours
Physical security and access control (ID, visitor log, CCTV)
Designated and equipped alternate EOC with relocation procedure
Redundant communications: VHF/UHF radio, HF, satellite phone, landline, mobile, internet (min. 3 independent channels)

indicators.statement: Radio network covering all 85 barangays and responders, with call signs and net-control procedure
Backup internet (secondary ISP/satellite) and continuity of digital systems
Communications plan/ directory (agencies, barangays, clusters) updated within last 6 months
Cybersecurity and information security measures for EOC systems
Display and monitoring equipment (video wall/monitors, weather feeds, CCTV feeds)
EOC organizational structure defined (EOC Manager, Operations, Planning/Information, Logistics, Admin/Finance, liaison desks)
Pre-designated EOC staff with alternates (at least 2 deep per key position)
Duty roster for sustained 24/7 operations with shift handover protocol
Agency/cluster liaison desks identified (CSWDO, CHO, CEO, PNP, BFP, AFP, DepEd, utilities, Red Cross)
Position checklists/job action sheets for each EOC role
Responder welfare in EOC: rest cycles, meals, MHPSS, family support
Standard SitRep/ Report templates aligned with NDRRMC/OCD formats and fixed reporting schedule
Barangay-to-city reporting flow (BDRRMC -> EOC) with defined timelines and formats
Common Operating Picture maintained (dashboard/ GIS map of incidents, evacuees, resources)
Evacuation center and affected-family tracking (DAFAC/ registration) feeds EOC data
EOC logbook/ significant events log and document retention
Weather/hazard monitoring routine (PAGASA, PHIVOLCS feeds) with bulletins logged and disseminated
Inbound citizen reporting (hotline, SMS, social media) feeds the common operating picture after a verification step
ICS-EOC interface defined: EOC supports Incident Commander(s); no duplication of command

indicators.statement: Resource management system: request, tracking, mobilization and demobilization of resources
Resource inventory (city, barangays, partners, private sector) accessible from EOC
Procedures for receiving and managing external assistance/ donations and volunteers
indicators.reference: NDRRMC guidelines on international/ external assistance

indicators.statement: Decision-support briefings to CDRRMC/Mayor at fixed intervals during activation
Pre-arranged resource commitments from partners and suppliers set out by item, quantity, activation trigger and contact in signed agreements (incl. supplier agreements tapped for anticipatory action)
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 1.2.4; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 6(a)(ii)

EOC staff trained (EOC operations course, ICS, IM) with records

Dedicated EOC budget for operations, maintenance and upgrades in LDRRMFIP
Equipment maintenance schedule and annual EOC readiness self-check

Risk-sensitive development guidelines applied in zoning and building permits, based on hazard maps
Structural safety of the EOC, evacuation centers and critical public facilities assessed by the Building Official, with a rapid safety inspection procedure before forecast impact
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 4.3.1, 4.4.2; PD 1096; RA 12076; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 4(c)(i)

Environmental anticipatory actions: declogging of waterways and drainage, slope stabilization, safe debris and carcass disposal

Education anticipatory action: schools' AA plans and learning-continuity modalities

# MOO Ch.1 – Legal and Institutional Framework

> Skeleton generated from IAT v1.1. Replace each requirement with the City's procedure, standard or form.

## Requirements this section must meet

- **A1.1** (M, weight 3) City ordinance/EO creating the CDRRMO as a regular office (not ad hoc), with defined functions mirroring RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12; IRR Rule 6; JMC 2014-1
- **A1.2** (M, weight 2) CDRRMC constituted with complete membership per RA 10121 Sec. 11 (incl. CSO and private sector reps)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 11
- **A1.3** (M, weight 2) CDRRMC meets at least quarterly (and as needed); minutes and resolutions on file  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 11; GKS/SGLG functionality criteria
- **A1.5** (GP, weight 2) Local DRRM-related ordinances in force (e.g., pre-emptive/forced evacuation, no-build zones, hazard-based zoning)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(19); RA 7160; CLUP/ZO
- **A1.6** (M, weight 3) Protocol for declaring a State of Calamity, incl. CDRRMC recommendation steps and post-declaration measures (State of Imminent Disaster now assessed separately under A1.8)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 16
- **A1.7** (GP, weight 1) DRRM is represented in City Development Council and Local Finance Committee deliberations  
  *Basis:* RA 7160; JMC 2013-1
- **A1.8** (M, weight 3) State of Imminent Disaster procedure: CDRRMC coordinates with RDRRMC VIII when the pre-disaster risk assessment shows reasonable certainty of severe impact; request format to RDRRMC (24-hour reply); Mayor's EO template; adoption rule when the Region (or Province, applicability to an ICC to be confirmed) is declared; lifting grounds and authority  
  *Basis:* RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 6; Rule III Secs. 2-4

> Skeleton generated from IAT v1.1. Replace each requirement with the City's procedure, standard or form.

## Requirements this section must meet

- **A3.1** (M, weight 3) Local DRRM Plan (LDRRMP) current, approved by Sanggunian, aligned with NDRRMP 2020-2030 and Sendai Framework  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); NDRRMP 2020-2030
- **A3.2** (M, weight 2) DRR-CCA mainstreamed in CDP, CLUP, ELA and LCCAP (hazard data used in land use and investment decisions)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 2; RA 9729 as amended by RA 10174; HLURB/DHSUD CLUP guidelines
- **A3.3** (M, weight 3) Hazard-specific Contingency Plans for priority hazards (flood/flash flood, landslide, earthquake/tsunami, tropical cyclone, industrial/geothermal), updated and tested  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC CP guidelines; OCD CP Manual
- **A3.4** (M, weight 2) Public Service Continuity Plan (PSCP) prepared covering CDRRMO and essential city services  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC/OCD PSCP Guidebook
- **A3.7** (GP, weight 2) Barangay DRRM plans (85 barangays) reviewed/consolidated by CDRRMO  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); DILG MC on BDRRM
- **A5.1** (M, weight 3) Updated hazard maps for all priority hazards (MGB, PHIVOLCS, PAGASA, GeoRiskPH/HazardHunterPH) at barangay scale  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(3); NDRRMP
- **A5.2** (M, weight 3) Climate & Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA)/ CRA completed with exposure (population, buildings, critical facilities) and vulnerability data  
  *Basis:* DHSUD/CCC CDRA guidelines; RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(3)
- **A5.3** (M, weight 2) Disaggregated population database (sex, age, disability, IP, pregnant/lactating) for at-risk households  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(5); RA 9710; RA 7277 as amended; RA 10821
- **A5.8** (GP, weight 2) Critical facilities list (EOC, hospitals, evacuation centers, water, power, telecom, bridges, port) with dependencies mapped as potential failure chains and used to set protection and restoration priorities  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.3.1; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule I Sec. 5(b),(d)
- **A7.6** (M, weight 2) Inclusive DRRM: GAD, PWD, senior citizen, children, IP considerations embedded in plans and services, with vulnerable-sector representatives confirming they were engaged  
  *Basis:* RA 9710; RA 7277 as amended; RA 9994; RA 10821; RA 8371; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 1(a); UNDRR DRSC 7.2.2
- **C1.1** (GP, weight 2) Most-probable and most-severe risk scenarios inform CDP/CLUP priorities and the location of major investments  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 1.1.1; RA 10121 Sec. 2; DHSUD CLUP guidelines
- **C1.2** (GP, weight 1) DRR/CCA screening step in project and budget approval (LDC, LFC)  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 1.3.1; climate change expenditure tagging guidelines
- **C1.3** (GP, weight 1) CDRA estimates losses beyond physical assets: livelihoods and jobs, housing and displacement, agriculture, ecosystems, cultural heritage  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.2.2; DHSUD/CCC CDRA guidelines
- **C1.4** (GP, weight 2) Risk-sensitive development guidelines applied in zoning and building permits, based on hazard maps  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.4.1; CLUP/ZO
- **C3.1** (GP, weight 2) Critical protective ecosystems (upper Anilao-Malbasag watershed, upland forest cover, coastal mangroves) identified and monitored as risk-reduction assets  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 5.1.1; RA 9729 as amended

  *Basis:* RA 10121; RA 12076; DILG Operation L!sto
- **A6.1** (M, weight 3) Hazard-specific EWS operational for flood (incl. Anilao/Malbasag river systems), rain-induced landslide, tsunami (Ormoc Bay) and tropical cyclone  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(8); PAGASA/PHIVOLCS protocols
- **A6.3** (M, weight 3) Last-mile dissemination channels tested to barangay/purok level (sirens, radio, SMS/ECBS, social media, barangay criers)  
  *Basis:* RA 10639 (Free Mobile Disaster Alerts); NDRRMC EWS
- **A6.4** (GP, weight 2) Warnings issued in local language (Cebuano/ Ormocanon) and accessible formats (sign language, visual alerts for PWD)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121; RA 11106 (FSL Act); RA 7277
- **A6.7** (M, weight 2) Templates and channels for public notice of a State of Imminent Disaster and of the anticipatory actions required, incl. sector-specific impact-based advisories and reach to geographically isolated barangays  
  *Basis:* RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 2
- **A7.4** (M, weight 3) Permanent evacuation center(s) planned/established and existing ECs meet minimum standards (WASH, privacy, PWD access, child-friendly space)  
  *Basis:* RA 12076 (Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act); RA 10821; DSWD standards
- **A7.6** (M, weight 2) Inclusive DRRM: GAD, PWD, senior citizen, children, IP considerations embedded in plans and services, with vulnerable-sector representatives confirming they were engaged

- **A7.9** (GP, weight 2) BDRRMCs can account for residents of affected puroks within 12 hours of impact (welfare check), shown in a drill or a real event  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 7.2.1
- **A8.1** (M, weight 3) Incident Command System institutionalized: EO on ICS, trained IMT roster, pre-designated Incident Commanders  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC MC No. 4, s. 2012 (ICS)
- **A8.2** (M, weight 3) Organized and trained response teams: SAR (WASAR/CSSR/HAZMAT as relevant), EMS/ambulance, fire coordination with BFP  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(16); RA 11589 (BFP)
- **A8.3** (M, weight 2) Response equipment and vehicles inventoried, serviceable and maintained (preventive maintenance schedule)  
  *Basis:* COA property rules; RA 10121
- **A8.7** (M, weight 2) Management of the Dead and Missing (MDM) and Rapid Damage Assessment & Needs Analysis (RDANA) teams designated and trained  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC MDM & RDANA guidelines
- **A8.8** (M, weight 3) Anticipatory action protocols by hazard and lead time: office-order templates for prepositioning (relief, medical supplies, animal feed, water and power for evacuation centers), deployment of heavy equipment, transport and personnel, pre-emptive evacuation incl. livestock and pets, CCCM, and safeguarding of critical infrastructure; aligned with CPs, Oplan L!sto and evacuation plans  
  *Basis:* RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Secs. 1, 3, 4, 6
- **A8.9** (M, weight 2) Anticipatory social amelioration: families identified and prioritized using CBMS or the prevailing registry; data-sharing agreements compliant with RA 10173; local guidelines for anticipatory cash or vouchers issued with the CSWDO  
  *Basis:* RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 7; RA 11315 (CBMS); RA 10173
- **C2.1** (GP, weight 3) Structural safety of the EOC, evacuation centers and critical public facilities assessed by the Building Official, with a rapid safety inspection procedure before forecast impact  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 4.3.1, 4.4.2; PD 1096; RA 12076; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 4(c)(i)

  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 21; JMC 2013-1

  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 21; COA Circular 2012-002

  *Basis:* JMC 2013-1; COA AAR findings

# **CHAPTER 1**

# **LEGAL MANDATE, DRRM GOVERNANCE AND INSTITUTIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY**

ORMOC CITY DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT OFFICE (CDRRMO) AND EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER (EOC)

**Revised Working Draft**

Assessment-based

## **1. Introduction**

Disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) in Ormoc City requires an integrated institutional system that connects executive leadership, policy direction, technical management, operational coordination and community-level action. Its effectiveness depends not only on the existence of the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (CDRRMC), the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) and the Emergency Operations Center (EOC), but also on the clarity of their respective mandates, decision-making authority, functional relationships, accountability arrangements and operational interfaces.

This chapter establishes the legal, governance and institutional accountability framework for the City's CDRRMO and EOC. It defines how the City Government organizes, directs, coordinates, monitors and continuously improves its DRRM functions across normal operations, preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response and recovery.

The chapter adopts a systems-thinking perspective: disaster risk is understood as the consequence of interconnected hazards, exposure, vulnerability, institutional capacities and dependencies across social, economic, environmental and physical systems. Accordingly, the City's DRRM governance arrangements must operate as an integrated system rather than as a collection of independent offices, committees and emergency procedures.

The chapter also applies Total Quality Management (TQM) principles to institutional operations. These include process ownership, evidence-based decision-making, stakeholder participation, standardization, performance measurement, corrective action and continuous improvement.

The institutional provisions are informed by the [<u>Ormoc CDRRMO–EOC Institutional Assessment Tool v1.3</u>](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L47rIY58uwKWk75YyV7LDELpF5PoJknJ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108981648814069460632&rtpof=true&sd=true), particularly its nine assessment sheets.

The assessment is treated as a diagnostic baseline, not as a substitute for legal compliance verification or formal institutional approval.

**Management implication**: The priority is not simply to create more committees or issue additional policies. ### **1.2 Interpretation of institutional Maturity and Compliance**

The assessment methodology distinguishes institutional maturity from mandatory compliance. A domain may achieve a relatively high maturity index while remaining legally non-compliant because one or more mandatory requirements have not attained the required rating.

This distinction is particularly important for Ormoc:

- CDRRMO Legal Mandate and DRRM Governance (A1) has a maturity index of 2.59/4.00, but only 50% mandatory compliance.

- EOC Legal Basis and Concept of Operations (B1) has a maturity index of 1.85/4.00, but 0% mandatory compliance.

- The overall mandatory compliance rate is 39.4%, notwithstanding the combined maturity index of 2.18.

The implication is that institutional improvements must address both capability and compliance. A procedure that is practiced informally cannot automatically be treated as an established institutional control. Similarly, the existence of an executive order, organizational chart or operational facility does not establish compliance unless the relevant requirements are documented, approved, implemented and supported by evidence.

The assessment uses the following evidence-based maturity logic:

| **Rating** | **Maturity classification**  | **Institutional interpretation**                                                             |
|------------|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0          | Absent                       | No established arrangement.                                                                  |
| 1          | Initial / Ad hoc             | Practice depends on individuals and is not adequately documented.                            |
| 2          | Developing                   | Arrangement exists but is incomplete, outdated, unapproved or inconsistently implemented.    |
| 3          | Compliant / Established      | Applicable standards are met through approved documentation and demonstrated implementation. |
| 4          | Advanced / Institutionalized | Compliance is sustained, tested, reviewed and improved through documented learning.          |

For purposes of this MOO, a procedure shall not be considered fully institutionalized merely because it appears in the Manual. Its implementation must be demonstrated through records, operational outputs, verification and periodic review.

## **2. Purpose**

This chapter establishes the legal and institutional governance arrangements governing the CDRRMO, CDRRMC and EOC.

It aims to:

1.  Establish a clear and legally grounded division of authority among the Local Chief Executive, CDRRMC, CDRRMO and EOC.

2.  Define the institutional responsibilities, decision rights and accountability of participating City Government offices.

3.  Institutionalize transparent, inclusive and evidence-based DRRM governance.

4.  Establish procedures for CDRRMC meetings, resolutions, recommendations and action monitoring.

5.  Standardize the City's procedures for State of Calamity and State of Imminent Disaster declarations.

6.  Strengthen vertical and horizontal coordination among the City Government, barangays, national government agencies, neighbouring LGUs, CSOs, private-sector partners and humanitarian organizations.

7.  Establish process ownership, responsibility assignments and decision-making controls using the RACI framework.

8.  Embed risk-informed governance, quality assurance, performance monitoring and continuous improvement into institutional operations.

## **3. Scope and Application**

This chapter applies to the following institutional actors:

- Office of the City Mayor;

- CDRRMC and its Secretariat;

- CDRRMO Head and functional divisions;

- EOC Manager and EOC functional sections;

- Sangguniang Panlungsod;

- City Government departments, offices and units;

- BDRRMCs in all 85 barangays;

- National government agencies and regional DRRM institutions;

- Accredited CSOs, ACDVs, private-sector organizations and other partners.

Its provisions apply under three operating conditions:

| **Operating condition**                       | **Institutional focus**                                                                                                                                | **Primary governance mechanism**                                                  |
|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Normal operations                             | Risk reduction, institutional planning, preparedness, capacity development, monitoring and continuity.                                                 | CDRRMC oversight and CDRRMO management.                                           |
| Heightened preparedness / anticipatory action | Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment, warning-action decisions, resource readiness, anticipatory measures and possible State of Imminent Disaster declaration. | CDRRMC coordination, Mayor's executive authority and CDRRMO technical leadership. |
| Emergency operations                          | Incident coordination, situational awareness, resource mobilization, policy support and operational reporting.                                         | Activated EOC, Incident Management Team and designated response clusters.         |

The Manual applies to all hazards and emergencies within the City's jurisdiction, including hydrometeorological, geological, climate-related, technological and human-induced hazards, subject to applicable institutional mandates.

It shall be read together with the City's approved DRRM plans, contingency plans, Public Service Continuity Plan, climate and disaster risk assessment, development plans, land-use plans and other applicable local policies.

## **5. Systems-Thinking Framework for DRRM Governance**

### **5.1 Institutional System Architecture**

Ormoc City's DRRM governance shall operate as a connected system comprising five interdependent layers:

1.  **Executive governance**: Political leadership, statutory authority and executive decision-making.

2.  **Policy and oversigh**t: CDRRMC deliberation, policy direction, recommendations and monitoring.

3.  **Institutional management**: CDRRMO planning, technical management, administration and implementation.

4.  **Operational coordination**: EOC, ICS, response clusters and incident management arrangements.

5.  **Community and external interface:** BDRRMCs, CSOs, private-sector institutions, utilities, national agencies and neighbouring LGUs.

The architecture recognizes that information, authority and resources move through different pathways.

- Executive authority flows through legally established government structures.

- Technical information flows from monitoring institutions, technical offices and communities toward decision-makers.

- Operational instructions flow through the approved command and coordination arrangements.

- Resources flow through authorized mobilization and accountability mechanisms.

- Feedback and performance information flow back into planning, policy and institutional improvement.

The CDRRMO shall ensure that these pathways are connected but not conflated.

### **5.2 The CDRRMO–EOC Institutional Interface**

The assessment identifies the institutional interface as the weakest component, with a separate maturity index of 1.29/4.00.

This indicates that the problem is not limited to individual office capacity. It concerns the connections between institutional actors, their processes, information systems and decision-making arrangements.

The following operating distinctions shall therefore apply:

| Relationship with ICS    | Provides institutional support and coordinates preparedness arrangements                       | Supports the Incident Commander and Incident Management Team                              |
| Institutional continuity | Maintains permanent office functions                                                           | Operates under activation, deactivation and continuity arrangements                       |

The EOC shall not replace the CDRRMO. Nor shall it become an alternative command structure for field response.

The Incident Commander shall retain incident-level command authority under the applicable ICS arrangements. The EOC shall facilitate coordination, provide information, mobilize support and elevate decisions requiring executive action.

## **6. Governance Structure and Institutional Mandates**

### **6.1 City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council**

The CDRRMC shall serve as the City's principal DRRM policy-making, coordinating and oversight body under RA 10121.

Its composition and functions shall conform to Section 11 of the Act and its IRR.

The City shall maintain an updated Executive Order identifying the membership, institutional representation, designated alternates and coordination responsibilities of the Council.

The assessment identifies the following governance requirements:

- Updating the CDRRMC Executive Order;

- Meeting statutory CSO representation requirements, including at least four accredited CSO representatives;

- Including private-sector representation;

- Maintaining institutional representation rather than relying solely on individual appointments; and

- Reviewing the membership register annually.

The CDRRMC shall ensure representation from relevant City Government offices, national agencies, public safety institutions, CSOs, the private sector and other prescribed members.

Its principal functions shall include:

1.  Approving, monitoring and evaluating the Local DRRM Plan;

2.  Integrating DRR and climate change adaptation into local development plans and budgets;

3.  Providing strategic direction for DRRM programs and policies;

4.  Recommending pre-emptive and forced evacuation where warranted;

5.  Recommending a State of Calamity declaration to the appropriate local legislative authority;

6.  Coordinating anticipatory action under RA 12287;

7.  Mobilizing institutional and external resources;

8.  Monitoring the use of DRRM funds and other dedicated resources; and

9.  Reviewing institutional performance, assessment findings and corrective actions.

### **6.2 City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office**

The CDRRMO shall function as the City's permanent institutional and technical mechanism for DRRM.

In accordance with Section 12 of RA 10121, it shall be responsible for setting the direction, development, implementation and coordination of local DRRM programs.

Its responsibilities include:

- Risk assessment and local risk information management;

- Local DRRM planning and contingency planning;

- Multi-hazard early warning;

- Training, orientation and knowledge management;

- Resource and capability inventory;

- Coordination with communities, CSOs and private-sector partners;

- Emergency monitoring and mobilization;

- Organization and supervision of emergency response teams and ACDVs;

- Recovery coordination;

- CDRRMC Secretariat functions; and

- Preparation and reporting of DRRM plans, budgets and fund utilization.

The CDRRMO shall perform these responsibilities through its approved organizational structure and in coordination with other City Government offices.

### **6.3 Emergency Operations Center**

The EOC shall provide the City's centralized mechanism for operational coordination during emergencies.

The EOC shall:

1.  Maintain situational awareness;

2.  Consolidate, validate and disseminate incident information;

3.  Support CDRRMC and executive decision-making;

4.  Facilitate coordination among the Incident Management Team and response clusters;

5.  Coordinate resource requests and mobilization;

6.  Maintain incident and decision records;

7.  Facilitate vertical coordination with provincial and regional DRRM institutions, as applicable; and

8.  Support transition from response to recovery.

The EOC shall operate within the authority established by the Mayor and the approved institutional arrangements.

### **6.4 Office of the City Mayor**

The City Mayor shall exercise the powers and responsibilities vested in the Local Chief Executive under RA 7160, RA 10121, RA 12287 and other applicable laws.

The Mayor shall:

- Provide executive leadership and direction;

- Chair the CDRRMC;

- Authorize actions within statutory authority;

- Direct the mobilization of City Government offices and resources;

- Issue valid executive orders and administrative directives;

- Exercise the relevant declaration authority under RA 12287;

- Approve institutional arrangements within the scope of executive authority; and

- Elevate matters requiring legislative or higher-level government action.

The Mayor's executive authority shall remain distinct from the legislative authority of the Sangguniang Panlungsod.

### **6.5 Sangguniang Panlungsod**

The Sangguniang Panlungsod shall exercise its legislative and oversight responsibilities in accordance with RA 7160 and applicable DRRM legislation.

Its relevant functions include:

- Enacting the ordinance establishing or strengthening the CDRRMO;

- Approving the necessary organizational and budgetary measures;

- Considering CDRRMC recommendations for a State of Calamity declaration;

- Enacting relevant local DRRM ordinances;

- Exercising oversight over local DRRM policies and resource allocation; and

- Supporting the institutionalization of the City's resilience priorities.

Legal distinction: The declaration of a State of Calamity under Section 16 of RA 10121 is issued by the local sanggunian upon the recommendation of the LDRRMC, based on damage assessment and needs analysis. It is not simply a Mayor's Executive Order.

## **7. Institutional Governance Processes and Workflows**

The MOO shall define governance as a series of connected, controlled and measurable processes. Each process shall have:

- A defined trigger or initiating condition;

- A designated process owner;

- Responsible actors;

- A legally authorized decision-maker;

- Required inputs and evidence;

- Defined outputs and records;

- Escalation and exception procedures; and

- Performance and compliance indicators.

This approach ensures that governance decisions can be traced from initiation to approval, implementation, reporting and review.

### **7.1 Process 1: CDRRMC Governance and Policy Decision-making**

**Purpose**: Ensure that DRRM policies, plans, priorities and institutional decisions are deliberated, approved or recommended by the appropriate authority and translated into accountable actions.

**Workflow GOV-01: CDRRMC Governance**

1.  **Initiation and agenda development**  
    > CDRRMO identifies policy issues, assessment findings, risk developments and matters requiring Council action.

2.  **Technical preparation**  
    > Concerned offices submit technical papers, evidence, financial implications and recommendations.

3.  **Secretariat processing  
    > **CDRRMO consolidates agenda items, issues meeting notices and circulates supporting documents.

4.  **Council deliberation  
    > **CDRRMC members review evidence, assess implications and deliberate on proposed actions.

5.  **Decision and documentation**  
    > The Council approves matters within its authority or adopts recommendations for submission to the appropriate approving authority.

6.  **Implementation and assignment  
    > **The Secretariat records decisions, assigns action owners and establishes target dates.

7.  **Monitoring and feedback  
    > **CDRRMO tracks implementation and reports unresolved actions at succeeding meetings.

**Required Output**

Approved minutes, resolutions or recommendations, decision register and action-monitoring report.

**Operating Requirements**

| **Control point**    | **Required standard**                                                                                                     |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### **7.4 Process 4: State of Calamity Declaration**

The City shall maintain a documented protocol consistent with Section 16 of RA 10121 and its IRR.

A State of Calamity declaration is based on the results of damage assessment and needs analysis. It shall be distinguished from the anticipatory declaration mechanism under RA 12287.

**Workflow GOV-04: State of Calamity**

1.  **Incident assessment**  
    > BDRRMCs, response agencies and the CDRRMO report casualties, affected populations, infrastructure damage, livelihood disruption and service interruptions.

2.  **RDANA consolidation**  
    > CDRRMO coordinates the validation and consolidation of damage and needs information.

3.  **Technical recommendation  
    > **CDRRMO prepares the assessment and submits it to the CDRRMC.

4.  **CDRRMC deliberation**  
    > The Council evaluates the evidence and adopts a recommendation where the legal criteria are met.

5.  **Legislative declaration  
    > **The Sangguniang Panlungsod considers and issues the declaration or lifting through the appropriate resolution.

6.  **Implementation  
    > **The City Government implements applicable remedial measures, resource arrangements, assistance and reporting requirements.

7.  **Monitoring and lifting  
    > **The CDRRMO monitors continuing impacts and prepares the technical basis for recommending lifting when appropriate.

**Required Outputs**

RDANA, CDRRMC recommendation, Sangguniang Panlungsod resolution, implementation records and lifting documentation.

The City shall maintain the following supporting records:

- Technical assessment and recommendation;

- RDANA and other supporting reports;

- CDRRMC resolution;

- Sangguniang Panlungsod resolution;

- Post-declaration action register;

- Resource utilization and accountability records; and

- Lifting recommendation and corresponding resolution.

The protocol shall also address coordination where national or regional declarations, infrastructure closures or emergency restrictions affect Ormoc City without automatically constituting a local State of Calamity declaration.

### **7.5 Process 5: State of Imminent Disaster Declaration and Anticipatory Action**

**New statutory Governance Process**

RA 12287 establishes a mechanism for declaring a State of Imminent Disaster before a disaster occurs, based on the applicable forecast, pre-disaster risk assessment and legal criteria.

The IRR released on 29 September 2026 provides the implementing framework for this mechanism.

The assessment identifies A1.8 as a mandatory requirement with a score of 1. The City has no localized procedure, request template or Mayor's Executive Order template documented in the evidence reviewed.

The following workflow shall therefore be institutionalized.

**Workflow GOV-05: State of Imminent Disaster**

1.  **Hazard forecast and trigger monitoring  
    > **CDRRMO Operations and Warning monitors official forecasts, advisories and hazard-specific triggers from PAGASA, PHIVOLCS and other competent agencies.

2.  **Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment  
    > **CDRRMO coordinates the assessment of exposure, vulnerability, projected severity, likely impacts, affected sectors, lead time and available response capacity.

3.  **Technical recommendation**  
    > CDRRMO prepares the PDRA findings and proposed anticipatory measures for CDRRMC consideration.

4.  **Regional coordination and recommendation  
    > **The City coordinates with RDRRMC VIII through OCD Region VIII and submits the prescribed request and supporting documentation.

5.  **Regional decision and response**  
    > RDRRMC VIII undertakes the action required under the Act and IRR. The request, acknowledgment and prescribed response timeline are documented.

6.  **Local declaration**  
    > Upon the applicable recommendation, the City Mayor may declare a State of Imminent Disaster through an Executive Order covering the jurisdiction forecast to be affected.

7.  **Activation of anticipatory measures**  
    > Authorized offices implement approved early actions, including pre-positioning, evacuation, protection of critical infrastructure and targeted social assistance.

8.  **Funding and accountability  
    > **Budget, Accounting, Procurement and implementing offices document commitments, disbursements, utilization and outputs in accordance with the IRR and applicable DBM-COA rules.

9.  **Lifting and post-declaration reporting  
    > **The City observes the applicable lifting procedures and submits the required post-lifting report to OCD within the prescribed 45-day period.

The process shall observe the following safeguards:

1.  A forecast alone shall not automatically trigger a declaration. The applicable legal criteria and PDRA requirements must be met.

2.  The CDRRMO shall provide technical recommendations, not independently exercise the declaration authority.

3.  The local declaration shall follow the recommendation and coordination mechanism prescribed by RA 12287 and its IRR.

4.  Anticipatory actions shall be proportionate to the projected impacts, hazard lead time, available resources and applicable legal authority.

5.  Measures shall observe inclusion, protection, do-no-harm and no-regrets principles.

6.  The use of funds shall follow the statutory funding limits, tranche arrangements and applicable financial regulations.

7.  Decisions, approvals, actions and expenditures shall be documented for audit and evaluation.

**Funding control**: As reflected in the assessment workbook, the IRR provides for an anticipatory-action allocation of up to 10% of the 70% LDRRMF component and a 30%/70% tranche arrangement associated with the prescribed three-day lead-time rule. The precise timing, eligibility, disbursement and documentation requirements must be implemented using the certified IRR and applicable DBM-COA guidance. The MOO shall not treat this allocation as an additional fund outside the statutory LDRRMF framework.

**Independent Component City clarification:** Ormoc's status as an Independent Component City must be considered when establishing its vertical coordination arrangements. The City shall obtain written confirmation from OCD Region VIII on the application of the IRR's regional and provincial coordination provisions, particularly whether any provincial declaration has legal applicability to Ormoc. The City's ICC status shall not be used as a reason to bypass the RDRRMC recommendation mechanism expressly established by RA 12287.

### **7.6 Process 6: Institutional Escalation and Inter-agency Coordination**

Institutional escalation shall occur when:

- The scale of an incident exceeds the capacity of a barangay;

- Multiple barangays require coordinated intervention;

- City resources are insufficient;

- Specialized national or regional assistance is required;

- Critical infrastructure or essential services are disrupted; or

- A statutory declaration or executive decision is necessary.

RA 10121, Section 15, provides the general coordination framework: barangay-level leadership where a barangay is affected, city/municipal leadership where two or more barangays are affected, and progressively higher coordination levels when impacts exceed the relevant territorial scale. Higher councils and institutions support the LGU's primary response responsibility.

The operational workflow shall be:

1.  Incident or risk information is reported to the appropriate local authority.

2.  The affected BDRRMC undertakes initial action and reports to the City.

3.  CDRRMO validates the information and assesses the level of support required.

4.  The CDRRMC and EOC coordinate City-wide institutional action, as appropriate.

5.  The City requests external assistance through the prescribed channels when required.

6.  The receiving institution acknowledges and assigns the request.

7.  The CDRRMO monitors the response and maintains the institutional record.

8.  Unresolved requirements are escalated through the appropriate higher-level coordination mechanism.

### **7.7 Process 7: Governance Review and Corrective Action**

All governance processes shall be subject to periodic review.

The CDRRMO shall:

1.  Consolidate compliance and performance information;

2.  Compare actual results against approved targets;

3.  Identify gaps, recurring problems and systemic causes;

4.  Assign corrective actions to accountable offices;

5.  Establish completion dates and required resources;

6.  Verify implementation;

7.  Report unresolved issues to the CDRRMC; and

8.  Update policies and procedures when necessary.

This process shall link the Institutional Assessment Tool, Action Plan, CDRRMC action register, annual LDRRMP monitoring and the MOO revision mechanism.

## **9. Total Quality Management and Institutional Performance**

### **9.1 Quality Management Approach**

The CDRRMO shall apply Total Quality Management principles to the design, implementation, monitoring and improvement of its governance processes.

TQM shall be treated as an institutional management approach rather than a separate administrative activity. Its purpose is to ensure that DRRM services are reliable, timely, accountable, evidence-based and responsive to the needs of affected communities.

The following principles shall guide implementation:

| **TQM principle**              | **Application to CDRRMO–EOC operations**                                                                                       |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Customer and stakeholder focus | Decisions and services shall respond to the needs of communities, affected populations, responders and institutional partners. |
| Leadership and accountability  | Each process shall have a designated owner and authorized decision-maker.                                                      |
| Process orientation            | Activities shall be standardized through workflows, SOPs, checklists and defined outputs.                                      |
| Systems approach               | Institutional processes shall be managed as interconnected functions rather than isolated activities.                          |
| Evidence-based decisions       | Decisions shall be supported by verified risk information, assessment results, operational reports and documented evidence.    |
| People engagement              | Personnel, barangays, CSOs and partners shall participate in process design, implementation and improvement.                   |
| Continuous improvement         | Findings from exercises, incidents, audits and assessments shall result in corrective and preventive action.                   |
| Relationship management        | Partnerships and institutional interfaces shall be actively maintained and evaluated.                                          |

### **9.2 Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) cycle**

The City shall apply the PDCA cycle as the primary mechanism for institutional quality improvement.

Institutional quality management cycle

# **PLAN**

Establish standards

Identify risks, set targets, assign owners, approve procedures and allocate resources.

# **DO**

Implement processes

Execute SOPs, coordinate actors, document outputs and deliver services.

# **CHECK**

Measure performance

Monitor indicators, verify compliance, review records and evaluate results.

# **ACT**

Correct and improve

Address root causes, revise procedures, assign corrective actions and retest improvements.

The PDCA cycle shall operate continuously across all CDRRMO and EOC functional modules.

The following templates shall be included in the MOO annexes:

- GOV-F01 – CDRRMC Membership and Designation Register;

- GOV-F02 – CDRRMC Meeting Notice and Agenda;

- GOV-F03 – CDRRMC Attendance and Minutes;

- GOV-F08 – State of Calamity Recommendation and Resolution;

- GOV-F13 – Post-Lifting 45-Day Report;

- GOV-F14 – Institutional RACI Register;

- GOV-F15 – Corrective and Preventive Action Register;

- GOV-F16 – Legal and Policy Register.

All templates shall have document identifiers, version numbers, approval status, responsible custodian and review dates.

## **13. Governance Controls, Documentation and Records Management**

The CDRRMO shall establish a controlled documentation system to ensure that institutional decisions and procedures remain accessible, authentic, traceable and current.

### **13.1 Document Control**

Each controlled document shall contain:

- Document title and code;

- Version and revision number;

- Date of preparation;

- Prepared-by and reviewed-by designations;

- Approving authority;

- Effective date;

- Revision history; and

- Distribution and access classification.

Only approved versions shall be used as official operational references.

### **13.2 Records Management**

The CDRRMO Secretariat shall maintain the official governance records in coordination with the City Records Officer.

Records shall be classified into:

1.  Legal and policy records;

2.  CDRRMC governance records;

3.  Institutional organizational records;

4.  Declaration and executive decision records;

5.  Financial and resource accountability records;

6.  Coordination and partnership records;

7.  Performance and audit records; and

8.  Corrective action and improvement records.

Retention and disposition shall follow applicable government records management and archival requirements.

### **13.3 Data Protection and Information Sharing**

The CDRRMO shall coordinate with the City's Data Protection Officer and information technology office to establish appropriate safeguards for DRRM information.

The system shall distinguish:

- Publicly available risk and preparedness information;

- Internal institutional information;

- Restricted operational information;

- Personal information of affected populations;

- Sensitive personal information; and

- Confidential personnel and security records.

The EOC shall use aggregated and appropriately anonymized information for operational dashboards whenever personal identifiers are not required.

Data sharing with CSWDO, CPDO, national agencies, barangays and partners shall be governed by appropriate data-sharing agreements and privacy safeguards under RA 10173.

## **14. Implementation, Review and Institutional Assurance**

### **14.1 Institutional Ownership**

The CDRRMO Head shall be the overall process owner for the implementation of this chapter, under the administrative authority of the Local Chief Executive and the policy oversight of the CDRRMC.

The City Legal Office, HRMO, Budget Office, Accounting Office, Secretariat and other concerned institutions shall discharge their assigned responsibilities.

### **14.2 Review Schedule**

| **Review activity**              | **Frequency**                                      | **Responsible owner**      |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| CDRRMC membership review         | Annually and after material organizational changes | CDRRMO                     |
| Governance SOP review            | Annually and after significant policy changes      | CDRRMO Head                |
| Legal and policy register review | At least annually                                  | CDRRMO / City Legal Office |
| RACI and delegation review       | Annually and after structural changes              | CDRRMO / HRMO              |
| CDRRMC performance review        | Quarterly, with annual consolidation               | CDRRMC Secretariat         |
| Institutional assessment         | Annually, or after major institutional changes     | CDRRMO                     |
| CAPA review                      | Quarterly                                          | CDRRMO Head                |
| MOO revision                     | Annually or when necessary                         | CDRRMO Head                |

### **14.3 Institutional Assurance**

The implementation of this chapter shall be evaluated through three complementary tests:

Compliance test: Are statutory and regulatory requirements met?

Effectiveness test: Do institutional arrangements produce timely, coordinated and reliable decisions and outputs?

Sustainability test: Are the arrangements institutionalized, documented, resourced, tested and capable of surviving leadership and personnel changes?

A governance process shall be considered effective only when it satisfies all three dimensions appropriate to its function.

# **15. Technical Validation Notes and Outstanding Decisions**

The following matters should be resolved before Chapter 1 is submitted for formal approval.

Two important corrections incorporated into this revised chapter:

1.  A State of Calamity is declared by the local sanggunian upon CDRRMC recommendation, not simply through a Mayor's Executive Order.

2.  A State of Imminent Disaster is a separate anticipatory mechanism under RA 12287. The Local Chief Executive may declare it through an Executive Order upon the prescribed Regional DRRM Council recommendation.

These distinctions are essential to legal compliance.

## **16. Relationship with the Succeeding Chapters**

To avoid duplication and maintain a coherent Manual, the following division of responsibilities is recommended:

| 1           | Legal Mandate, DRRM Governance and Institutional Accountability         | A1, B1.1, C1–C5 interfaces          |
| 2           | CDRRMO Organizational Structure, Staffing and Human Resource Management | A2, B4                              |
| 3           | Risk Intelligence, Planning and Institutional Preparedness              | A3, A5, relevant Part C indicators  |
| 4           | Early Warning, Activation, Incident Management and Emergency Response   | A6, A7, A8, B1.2–B1.5               |
| 5           | DRRM Financing, Procurement and Resource Accountability                 | A4                                  |
| 6           | EOC Operations, Information Management, Logistics and Coordination      | B2–B7, relevant A indicators        |
| 7           | Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge Management and Continuous Improvement | A5.4–A5.9, A10                      |
| 8           | Recovery, Rehabilitation and Build Back Better                          | A9                                  |
| 9           | Partnerships, Local Ownership and Institutional Sustainability          | A10, relevant Part C indicators     |

This structure should be reconciled with the ten functional areas in Annex A and the eight contractual functional modules. The chapter numbering is a proposed detailed document architecture, not a change to the contractual scope.

## **16. Concluding Notes**

This chapter establishes the legal, institutional and governance foundation for the integrated operation of Ormoc City's CDRRMC, CDRRMO and EOC.

It recognizes that urban resilience is not produced by a single office or emergency facility. It emerges from the effective interaction of executive leadership, institutional capacity, policy coordination, risk information, financial governance, community participation and operational systems.

The institutional assessment demonstrates that Ormoc has established important DRRM governance practices, particularly regular CDRRMC meetings, Secretariat functions, DRRM representation in development and financial bodies, and existing planning and partnership mechanisms. However, gaps in legal institutionalization, EOC authority, anticipatory governance and cross-office coordination continue to constrain the effectiveness of the wider system.

The provisions of this chapter respond to these issues by establishing:

- Clear institutional mandates and decision rights;

- Defined process ownership and responsibility assignments;

- Standardized governance workflows;

- Legally differentiated declaration procedures;

- Formalized institutional and inter-agency interfaces;

- RACI-based accountability;

- TQM and PDCA-based quality assurance; and

- Evidence-based monitoring and continuous improvement.

The ultimate objective is to move Ormoc City's DRRM governance from arrangements that are partly dependent on individual initiative toward a legally grounded, process-driven, integrated and continuously improving institutional system.

This foundation shall support the implementation of the succeeding modules, particularly organizational management, preparedness, EOC operations, information management, resource mobilization, recovery and performance improvement.

# ANNEX 1-A \| PROPOSED ORDINANCE – CDRRMO INSTITUTIONALIZATION

**PROPOSED – FOR LEGAL / TECHNICAL REVIEW**

Document status: Draft instrument. This text is a drafting aid and must be checked against the latest certified statutes, implementing rules, local organizational structure, approved plantilla, budget, and applicable City procedures before signature or enactment.

## AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AND STRENGTHENING THE CITY DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT OFFICE OF ORMOC CITY, DEFINING ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, FUNCTIONS AND ACCOUNTABILITY, PROVIDING FOR COORDINATION WITH THE CDRRMC AND EOC, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

BE IT ORDAINED by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Ormoc City, in session assembled, that:

## Section 1. Short Title.

This Ordinance shall be known as the “Ormoc City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office Institutionalization Ordinance.”

## Section 2. Declaration of Policy.

The City shall maintain a permanent, adequately staffed, technically competent and accountable CDRRMO consistent with RA 10121, its IRR, JMC No. 2014-1 and applicable local government, civil service and budget rules.

## Section 3. Establishment and Status.

The CDRRMO is hereby established or, if already established by prior valid issuance, strengthened and institutionalized as a regular office of the City Government. The City Legal Office shall determine whether this is a new or amendatory ordinance after reviewing existing issuances.

## Section 4. Organizational Structure.

The CDRRMO shall be headed by a duly qualified CDRRMO Head and maintain the functional areas required by applicable national guidelines: Administration and Training; Research and Planning; and Operations and Warning. Additional units and positions require approval under DBM, CSC and City processes.

## Section 5. Functions.

The CDRRMO shall lead and coordinate local DRRM planning and implementation; risk information; contingency planning; early warning; training; preparedness; response coordination; recovery support; CDRRMC Secretariat functions; reporting; and institutional performance improvement, consistent with RA 10121.

## Section 6. Relationship with CDRRMC and EOC.

The CDRRMC remains the City's statutory policy-making, coordinating and oversight body. The CDRRMO is its permanent technical and administrative office. The EOC is an operational coordination mechanism established through a separate executive issuance. It does not replace the CDRRMO or field ICS command.

## Section 7. Coordination and non-duplication.

The CDRRMO shall coordinate with City offices, barangays, national agencies, utilities, CSOs and private-sector partners, but shall not assume technical, regulatory, fiduciary or statutory functions assigned to other offices.

## Section 8. Staffing and qualifications.

HRMO and CDRRMO shall prepare staffing, qualification standards and position descriptions for review under applicable CSC and DBM rules. No position is created beyond an approved plantilla and lawful appropriation.

## Section 9. Funding.

Funding shall be sourced from lawful appropriations and eligible DRRM funds, subject to RA 10121, LDRRMF guidelines, budgeting, accounting, procurement and audit rules. This Ordinance does not independently authorize a particular allocation or expenditure.

## Section 10. Implementing procedures.

The CDRRMO shall maintain the CDRRMO–EOC Manual of Operations and implementing procedures, subject to legal review and approval by the competent authority.

## Section 11. Separability.

If any provision is declared invalid, the remaining provisions shall remain effective.

## Section 12. Repealing / amending clause.

Inconsistent local issuances are amended or repealed only to the extent of inconsistency, subject to identification by the City Legal Office.

## Section 13. Effectivity.

This Ordinance shall take effect in accordance with the Local Government Code and applicable approval, posting and publication requirements.

## Section 1. Establishment.

The City EOC is established as an operational coordination mechanism administered by the CDRRMO and activated under approved triggers and procedures.

## Section 2. Functions.

The EOC maintains situational awareness; validates and disseminates incident information; supports executive and CDRRMC decision-making; coordinates resource requests; facilitates inter-office and inter-agency coordination; maintains incident and decision records; and supports transition to recovery.

## Section 3. Non-command status.

The EOC is not a field command structure. The Incident Commander retains incident-level command under applicable ICS arrangements. EOC coordination does not alter agency mandates or operational control.

The CDRRMO Head oversees readiness. A designated EOC Manager manages activated operations under approved job action sheets and reporting lines.

Activation may be triggered by official warnings, PDRA findings, actual or imminent impacts, multi-barangay incidents, critical service disruption, resource coordination needs or direction of the Mayor / authorized official. The MOO shall specify levels and authority.

The authorized official shall deactivate the EOC when coordination needs have sufficiently reduced and transition arrangements are established. Closure includes logs, resource reconciliation and after-action review.

The CDRRMO shall maintain duty rosters, contact directories, handover procedures, communications redundancy, facility checklists and minimum staffing arrangements, subject to approved resources.

## Section 8. Information and records.

The EOC shall maintain incident logs, situation reports, decision logs, resource records and dashboards subject to privacy, security, records and disclosure requirements.

# ANNEX 1-D \| SOP GOV-04 – STATE OF CALAMITY

**PROPOSED – FOR LEGAL / TECHNICAL REVIEW**

Document status: Draft instrument. This text is a drafting aid and must be checked against the latest certified statutes, implementing rules, local organizational structure, approved plantilla, budget, and applicable City procedures before signature or enactment.

## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE GOV-04: STATE OF CALAMITY DECLARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND LIFTING

Purpose. To establish a documented procedure consistent with Section 16 of RA 10121 and its IRR.

Critical authority rule. The local sanggunian declares or lifts a State of Calamity upon recommendation of the LDRRMC, based on damage assessment and needs analysis. A Mayor's Executive Order shall not substitute for the Sanggunian's statutory declaration.

| **Control**        | **Requirement**                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Process owner      | CDRRMO Head                                                                                                                                   |
| Recommendation     | CDRRMC, based on validated assessment                                                                                                         |
| Decision authority | Sangguniang Panlungsod, as provided by law                                                                                                    |
| Core evidence      | RDANA; affected population; casualties; infrastructure / livelihood damage; service interruption; urgent needs; response capacity             |
| Records            | Assessment, Council minutes / recommendation, Sanggunian resolution, implementation and resource records, lifting recommendation / resolution |

### Procedure

Receive and log reports from BDRRMCs, response agencies, utilities and City offices; record source, time, location and verification status.

1\. Receive and log reports from BDRRMCs, response agencies, utilities and City offices; record source, time, location and verification status.

2\. Conduct and consolidate RDANA using approved methodology and competent sector offices; distinguish verified facts, estimates and information gaps.

3\. Prepare a technical assessment describing scale, severity, affected sectors, urgent needs, available capacity and basis for or against recommending declaration.

4\. Submit assessment to CDRRMC for deliberation and recommendation where statutory criteria are met.

5\. Transmit complete recommendation and evidence package to the Sangguniang Panlungsod for action through the legally prescribed process.

6\. Upon valid Sanggunian resolution, implement authorized remedial measures, assistance and reporting.

7\. Maintain post-declaration action register and monitor impacts, service restoration, resources and outstanding needs.

8\. When warranted, recommend lifting; the Sanggunian shall act through the applicable legal process.

9\. Archive the decision trail and conduct an after-action review.

Required records: incident report; RDANA; CDRRMC attendance, minutes and recommendation; Sanggunian resolution; action and resource register; public information; lifting recommendation and resolution. CLO shall verify statutory criteria, current IRR, resolution form, publication/posting and lifting process.

## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE GOV-05: STATE OF IMMINENT DISASTER DECLARATION, ANTICIPATORY ACTION, LIFTING AND POST-LIFTING REPORTING

Purpose. To establish a controlled process under RA 12287 and its certified IRR for PDRA, regional recommendation, local declaration, anticipatory action, lifting and reporting.

Critical authority rule. A forecast alone does not automatically justify declaration. Statutory criteria, PDRA requirements and prescribed recommendation / coordination mechanism must be met. The Mayor's declaration authority shall be exercised only after all legal prerequisites are confirmed.

| **Control**              | **Requirement**                                                                                            |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Process owner            | CDRRMO Head                                                                                                |
| Technical lead           | CDRRMO Operations and Warning with sector offices                                                          |
| Regional interface       | OCD Region VIII / RDRRMC VIII, subject to certified IRR                                                    |
| Local decision authority | City Mayor, through EO only after prescribed recommendation                                                |
| Funding                  | Budget / Accounting / Procurement subject to certified IRR and DBM / COA rules                             |
| Reporting                | Post-lifting deadline as prescribed by certified IRR; 45 days reported in assessment and must be confirmed |

### Procedure

1\. Monitor official forecasts and advisories from PAGASA, PHIVOLCS and other competent authorities; log source, issue time, validity, geography and lead time.

2\. Initiate PDRA when hazard-specific triggers warrant; assess exposure, vulnerability, projected severity, cascading impacts, sectoral needs, critical facilities, lead time and response capacity.

3\. Obtain sector inputs from health, social welfare, agriculture, engineering, utilities, education, transport, environment and barangays as relevant.

4\. Prepare PDRA summary, proposed anticipatory measures, resource requirements, funding source, implementation owners, safeguards and indicators.

5\. Convene CDRRMC or its authorized mechanism to review evidence and endorse the City's request, without substituting for the statutory regional recommendation.

6\. Coordinate with OCD Region VIII / RDRRMC VIII through the certified IRR route; log request, attachments, receipt, clarifications, recommendation and official response.

7\. After confirmation of prerequisites, prepare the Mayor's EO specifying hazard, covered areas, validity, authorized measures, responsible offices, resource controls and reporting.

8\. Implement only approved and legally authorized actions, which may include prepositioning, early evacuation, critical infrastructure protection, continuity measures and targeted assistance.

9\. Maintain action logs, beneficiary records, procurement and disbursement records, coverage, outputs, complaints and safeguards. Apply RA 10173 safeguards.

10\. Monitor hazard and impacts; lift the declaration in the manner prescribed by law and document basis, effective time and transition arrangements.

11\. Prepare and submit required post-lifting report within deadline in certified IRR; assessment records a 45-day period, which must be verified.

12\. Conduct after-action review and update triggers, PDRA tools, SOP and corrective action register.

Mandatory hold points: CLO verifies certified RA 12287 IRR and recommendation route; OCD VIII confirms regional / provincial coordination applicability to Ormoc as an Independent Component City; Budget, Accounting, CLO and OCD verify reported allocation percentages and tranche rules against certified IRR and DBM/COA guidance; beneficiary data comply with RA 10173.

Required records: official forecast log; PDRA; sector inputs; CDRRMC records; regional request and acknowledgment; recommendation; Mayor's EO; anticipatory action / expenditure logs; lifting documentation; post-lifting report; after-action review.
